clue.text: Refuse to allow amusement where Queen won't hear it?

definitions.meaning: to dismiss a claim or idea with ridicule, as a judge throws out a case

definitions.text: amusement where Queen won't hear it?
definitions.meaning: laughter taking place away from the royal court, so beyond the monarch's hearing

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the idiom literally: a laugh had outside the court, where the sovereign cannot hear it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to dismiss something with scorn as not worth a hearing, so it is a way to refuse to allow it.

clue.text: Liberal's coldness over new Church freedom

indicators.note: over puts the Liberal above the rest in a down answer

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
ice stands for coldness
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician's frosty attitude to the new Church freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Liberal's' is the link 'has' or 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A licence is a permission or liberty to act, a kind of freedom.

clue.text: Line grabbed by one in the dark

indicators.note: grabbed by means the line is held inside the other word

parts.note: a unit is one

explanation.surface: Someone seizes a fishing line in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlit means without light, so a place unlit is in the dark.

clue.text: Solidified cosmetic? One's rigorous in application

parts.note: hard means solidified, set
liner, as in eyeliner, is a cosmetic

explanation.surface: A make-up product that has set hard proves strict when applied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'application' suggests applying make-up; in the definition it means applying rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardliner is someone who sticks rigidly to a policy, applying it rigorously.

clue.text: Ruin a French party

parts.note: un is the French for a
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A French party ends in disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: To be someone's undoing is to ruin them; to undo is to bring to ruin.

clue.text: Passive love and fondness about to fade away

parts.note: O, zero, is love in tennis

indicators.note: about means the fondness word goes round the fading word

parts.note: a bent is a liking or inclination
to die away is to fade

explanation.surface: Love and affection seem to be fading away into passivity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the fading word inside the fondness word after its second letter; 'Passive' reads as grammar but means submissive.
explanation.definitionFit: An obedient person does as told without resisting, so is passive or submissive.

clue.text: Economy? That's an attractive thing

parts.note: a cut is an economy, a saving
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: An economy measure is presented as an appealing idea.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'That's' is part of the leaf: 'that is' gives IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutie is an attractive person, informally a cute thing.

clue.text: Complete article on church sermon, say

indicators.note: on places the church below the rest in a down answer

parts.note: utter means complete or total
an is the indefinite article
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A whole piece about the church is delivered as a sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: A sermon is an example of an utterance, something spoken aloud, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Warming element of smoother malt

indicators.note: element of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A smoother malt whisky has a warming quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermal relates to heat, so thermal clothing is warming.

clue.text: Exponent of art I'd found in El Greco, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters might be arranged in another order

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe giving no letter
the painter's name taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic spots a fine example of art in a painting by the Spanish master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is a link. The letters of I'D and EL GRECO, rearranged, give the poet's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romantic poet and critic Samuel Taylor Coleridge was a famous practitioner and theorist of poetic art.

clue.text: Championship match? Little time left in that

indicators.note: left means departed, so this letter goes out of the word

parts.note: a tittle is a tiny amount, a jot

explanation.surface: A title fight is entering its last moments, with the clock nearly run down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Championship match?' suggests a fight, but only 'Championship' defines; 'match?' and 'in that' add the boxing picture. Take T for time out of TITTLE (a jot) to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A title in sport is a championship held by the reigning winner, as in a world title.

clue.text: Upset sample of herbal tea?

definitions.meaning: to upset someone is to irritate or annoy them
a plant whose leaves are steeped to make an infusion

explanation.walkthrough: The stinging plant is used for a herbal infusion, so a leaf of it is a sample of that tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To nettle is to irritate or annoy, a verb sense of being upset; the plant is a common herbal tea ingredient.

clue.text: One's struck by player given odd days at first on team

indicators.note: on places the following pieces after the team in an across answer
at first puts the days ahead of the odd word

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
rum is an old-fashioned word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A footballer who has been picked to play on strange days is joining a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' puts the days ahead of the odd word, and 'on' sets both after the team; 'player' suggests sport but means a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A side drum is a small snare drum that a drummer strikes with sticks.

clue.text: Fur backed piece of denim revolutionary!

indicators.note: backed says the hidden letters are read backwards
piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fashion writer hails the trimmed-back denim jacket as revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: The run ENIMRE sits across 'denim revolutionary'; 'backed' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermine is the white winter coat of the stoat, prized as a fur for royal robes.

clue.text: Cinema venue? Mostly mused about suggestion supported by Times

indicators.note: supported by puts the times sign below the rest in a down answer
about means the shortened word goes round the suggestion
mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: mulled means pondered or mused
a tip is a suggestion
X is the multiplication sign for times

explanation.surface: Someone muses on a suggestion backed by the Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the last letter of the mused word, and 'about' wraps it round the suggestion; 'Times' is not the newspaper but the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A multiplex is a cinema complex with many screens, a venue for films.

clue.text: Hellish final battles involving English sailors

indicators.note: involving means the scrambled word wraps around the other pieces
battles suggests the word final is fought over and knocked into a new shape

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: A last battle at sea involves English sailors in a hellish fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battles' rearranges the printed word as INFAL, and 'involving' wraps it round the English sailors after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernal means belonging to the inferno, that is hell, so it is a synonym of hellish.

clue.text: Decorate heel and limbs with abandon

indicators.note: with abandon suggests a wild, unrestrained jumble of the letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dancer adorns the routine, flinging heels and limbs about freely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link joining the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: To embellish is to decorate or adorn something.

clue.text: Unfancied performer grounded after accident

indicators.note: after an accident something is wrecked, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer is laid up after a mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: An underdog is a competitor not expected to win, an unfancied contender.

clue.text: Location in Carmen — some nonsense linked to operatic extravaganza

parts.note: bull is slang for nonsense
the Ring is Wagner's vast four-opera cycle

explanation.surface: Set in Bizet's opera, some silly business is tied in with a lavish operatic show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'linked to' is a link. Bizet's Carmen ends outside a Seville bullring, where her lover kills her.
explanation.definitionFit: The bullring is a setting in the final act of the opera, where the toreador fights.

clue.text: First half of book by marvellous biographer

indicators.note: first half of picks the opening two of the word's four letters

parts.note: swell is slang for marvellous

explanation.surface: Read the first half of a book by a wonderful life writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: James Boswell wrote the celebrated Life of Samuel Johnson, the model of a biographer.

clue.text: Come down with cattle disease and feel bad about it

indicators.note: about it means the feeling-unwell word goes round the disease

parts.note: to ail is to feel unwell
BSE is bovine spongiform encephalopathy, mad cow disease

explanation.surface: Someone goes down with a cattle disease and feels guilty about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link; 'Come down' suggests falling ill, but it means descending a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To abseil is to come down a rock face or wall by sliding down a rope.

clue.text: Precise US quantity of liquid — short measure in beer?

parts.note: liter is the American spelling of the metric measure

indicators.note: short means the beer word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: ale is beer

explanation.surface: An American litre of beer seems to have been short-measured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'measure in' is linking the surface's complaint; the beer is short by one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal means exact, following the precise words, so it means precise.

clue.text: Period of work crucial — it produces capital

parts.note: a shift is a set period of work
key means crucial or vital

explanation.surface: A vital work shift turns out to be what earns money for the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests money, but here it is a capital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The shift key on a keyboard is held down to type capital letters.

clue.text: Garment's style involving fashionable turning up

indicators.note: turning up in a down answer means the pieces read from bottom to top
involving means the style word holds the fashion word

parts.note: the cut of clothes is their style
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A garment's style includes the fashionable trend of turned-up hems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' gives CINUT, and 'turning up' reads it backwards; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic is a loose garment reaching to the hips or knees.

clue.text: Recalled wall fitting containing one carbon extract

indicators.note: containing means the reversed fitting holds the other pieces
recalled means called back, so the fitting is read backwards

parts.note: a tile is fixed to a wall
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A recalled tiling product contains carbon, a worrying finding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' reads the fitting backwards as ELIT, and 'containing' puts one and carbon inside it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw out or extract information or a response from someone.

clue.text: Illness? Pass on one cold

indicators.note: on puts the pass above the rest in a down answer

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether passing on a cold counts as an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is severe abdominal pain, an illness especially in babies and horses.

clue.text: Centre of Nagasaki and borders of India featured here?

definitions.text: Centre of Nagasaki and borders of India featured here?

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle two letters of the city's name
borders of picks the first and last letters of the country

explanation.surface: A traveller wonders where both Nagasaki and India appear on the map.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the continent containing both places.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the continent where both Japan's Nagasaki and India lie.

clue.text: Girl implicitly embraced, by Greek?

indicators.note: the girl's name sits embraced inside a Greek word, implied rather than printed

parts.note: a Hellene is a Greek

explanation.surface: A girl is quietly hugged by a Greek man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link. HELLENE loses its first and last letters, leaving the girl's name held inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen is a common girl's name, standing for any girl.

clue.text: Drinks producer not making moves in long run

indicators.note: in places the motionless word inside the yearning word

parts.note: to long for something is to be dying for it, so long gives DIE
still means motionless
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A drinks firm is standing still when it should be planning for the long run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long run' reads as one phrase but splits into DIE (long, as in 'dying to') and R (run).
explanation.definitionFit: A distiller makes spirits such as whisky and gin, so is a producer of drinks.

clue.text: Giving meaning to life, inter alia

definitions.text: Giving meaning to life, inter alia

parts.words: Giving meaning to life, inter alia
parts.note: a philosophical phrase about purpose, read as a dictionary defining the word life among many others

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a purpose in existence; read literally, a dictionary gives the meaning of 'life' alongside other words.
explanation.definitionFit: Lexicographical work concerns compiling dictionaries, which give the meanings of words such as life.
